module_title: Specific Contracts: Indemnity, Guarantee, Bailment & Agency (Foundational)
introduction: This foundational level introduces the 'Specific Contracts' defined in Sections 124 to 238 of the Indian Contract Act (ICA), 1872. It demystifies the basic definitions, the number of parties involved, and the primary purpose of Indemnity, Guarantee, Bailment, and Agency.

core_concepts.title: Contract of Indemnity (Section 124)
core_concepts.description:
A contract by which one party promises to save the other from loss caused to them by the conduct of the promisor himself, or by the conduct of any other person.
- Parties: 2 (Indemnifier - who promises to make good the loss, and Indemnity-holder - whose loss is covered).
- Classic Example: All Insurance contracts (except life insurance) are contracts of indemnity.

core_concepts.title: Contract of Guarantee (Section 126)
core_concepts.description:
A contract to perform the promise, or discharge the liability, of a third person in case of their default.
- Parties: 3 (Surety - who gives the guarantee, Principal Debtor - for whose default the guarantee is given, and Creditor - to whom the guarantee is given).
- Purpose: It is fundamentally a contract of *security*. If the Principal Debtor fails to pay the Creditor, the Surety will pay.

core_concepts.title: Contract of Bailment (Section 148)
core_concepts.description:
The delivery of goods by one person to another for some purpose, upon a contract that they shall, when the purpose is accomplished, be returned or otherwise disposed of according to the directions of the person delivering them.
- Parties: 2 (Bailor - who delivers the goods, and Bailee - who receives them).
- Key Rule: Bailment involves a transfer of *possession*, NOT *ownership* (e.g., giving your car to a mechanic for repair, or parking a car in a paid lot).

core_concepts.title: Contract of Agency (Section 182)
core_concepts.description:
An 'Agent' is a person employed to do any act for another, or to represent another in dealings with third persons. The person for whom such act is done is called the 'Principal'.
- Legal Maxim: *Qui facit per alium, facit per se* (He who acts through another does the act himself).
- Purpose: The acts of the agent bind the principal as if the principal had done them personally.

important_entities.name: Pledge / Pawn (Section 172)
important_entities.significance: Pledge is the bailment of goods strictly as *security for payment of a debt or performance of a promise*. (e.g., giving your gold jewelry to a moneylender to get a loan). The bailor is the Pawnor; the bailee is the Pawnee.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners constantly test the structural difference between Indemnity and Guarantee. In Indemnity, there is only **1 contract** (between Indemnifier and Indemnity-holder). In Guarantee, there are **3 contracts**: (1) Creditor & Principal Debtor, (2) Surety & Creditor, and (3) Implied contract between Surety & Principal Debtor.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Indemnity (2 parties), Guarantee (3 parties), Bailment (2 parties), Agency (2 parties + deals with a 3rd party).

exam_strategy_tips: Whenever a question asks 'Which contract protects a person against loss caused strictly by human agency (conduct of promisor or other person)?', the answer is **Contract of Indemnity (Sec 124)**.
